name: Parmenion
bio: Parmenion is one of the epigrammatists whose short poems were gathered in the Greek Anthology. Paton's index of authors dates the poet to 1st century AD. Paton's index lists the poet among the writers of the Wreath of Philippus, the Garland compiled in the first century AD.
This archive carries the 3 epigrams ascribed to the poet in the second volume of W. R. Paton's prose translation (Book VII: 183, 184, 239).

poems.title: Book VII, 183
poems.author: Parmenion
poems.text: (As she had just loosed her maiden zone) Death came first and took the maidenhood of Crocale. The bridal song ended in wailing, and the fond anxiety of her parents was set to rest not by marriage but by the tomb.

poems.title: Book VII, 184
poems.author: Parmenion
poems.text: I am the tomb of the maiden Helen, and in mourning too for her brother who died before her I receive double tears from their mother. To her suitors I left a common grief; for the hope of all mourned equally for her who was yet no one’s.

poems.title: Book VII, 239
poems.author: Parmenion
poems.text: It is a lying report that Alexander is dead if Phoebus be true. Not even Hades can lay hand on the invincible.
